question.text: POEM (Place of Effective Management) is defined as the place where:

answer.text: The company is incorporated and its registered office is located
The majority of the company's employees are physically present
The company's manufacturing or operational facilities are situated
Key management and commercial decisions necessary for the conduct of business are, in substance, made

explanation.text: The Logic: Under Indian income-tax law, Place of Effective Management (POEM) is defined as the place where key management and commercial decisions that are necessary for the conduct of the business of an entity as a whole are, in substance, made. The emphasis on "in substance" means the test looks at where decisions are actually taken, not merely where board meetings are formally recorded or registers are kept. Place of incorporation fixes legal domicile but not POEM; the location of most employees, and the location of manufacturing or operational facilities, are operational data points and not the definition of POEM. The Trap: Incorporation, employee concentration, and operational facility locations are tempting because they are easy to observe — but POEM is specifically about where the controlling management and commercial decisions are substantively made. Note: The Place-of-Effective-Management definition (key management and commercial decisions in substance) is not stated on the NISM Series X-B Investment Adviser Level 2 workbook pages checked; the framing above reflects the definition in Section 6(3) of the Indian Income Tax Act and CBDT POEM guidelines rather than a workbook citation.
